chunks: From him, from Ibn Jَبَلَة, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The salat (prayer) in residence is eight rakʿahs when the sun declines; the time between you and the passing of two-thirds of a qāmah is for that. Then when two-thirds of a qāmah has passed, you begin with the obligatory prayer.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), here referring to the prescribed and recommended prayer units being discussed
key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: residence; being settled and not traveling
key_terms.ثَمَانِي رَكَعَاتٍ: eight units of prayer, referring here to the recommended rakʿahs before the obligatory prayer
key_terms.ثُلُثَا الْقَامَةِ: two-thirds of a qāmah, a proportional measure used to indicate prayer timing
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun declined from its zenith, marking the beginning of the prayer time

ai.seo_question: When should one perform the eight rakʿahs before the obligatory noon salat (prayer) in residence?
ai.summary: This hadith states the recommended time and measure for performing the supererogatory rakʿahs before the obligatory noon prayer while in residence. It indicates that after the sun’s decline, one may perform eight rakʿahs until the point marked by the passing of two-thirds of a qāmah, after which the obligatory salat (prayer) begins first.
